docs.arch_assets: The React app is served by the Worker's static assets binding, next to the /api routes.
docs.arch_cron: A cron trigger runs every minute. It returns snoozed mail that is due, seals mail that was waiting for its owner's keys, and converts old plaintext mail. It also applies two-factor resets that are due and, seven days after a person asked, deletes their locked old mail.
docs.arch_d1: Accounts, domains, settings, the audit log and the mail index live in D1. The index holds the sender, recipients, dates, sizes and labels in the clear; the subject, text and attachment names are sealed.
docs.arch_inbound: Cloudflare Email Routing hands each message to the Worker. For an address that belongs to an account it is sealed to that person's key and stored, or held under DATA_KEY until they have set up keys; any other address is rejected.
docs.arch_keys: Mail is sealed to each person's own key. {data_key} protects what the server must read back, including mail that arrives before a person has set up keys.
docs.arch_outbound: Mail to other servers leaves through Cloudflare Email Sending. Mail between people on this deployment is sealed in the sender's browser and does not leave, but only when every recipient has set up keys and the message is within the size limits. Otherwise the server can read it: a copy for somebody without keys is sent in the clear to the server, and a message that is too large goes the normal way, out through Email Sending and back in.
docs.arch_push: Devices with notifications on get a Web Push for new mail. It names the sender only, never the subject or text.
docs.arch_r2: Sealed raw messages and attachments live in R2.
docs.arch_realtime: A Durable Object (MailHub) holds each person's open WebSockets and tells their open tabs when mail changes. It sends ids, the sender and the time, never a subject or text.
docs.deploy_intro: Run these yourself, in this order, from a clone of the repository. The full guide is {deployment} and every setting is in {configuration}.
docs.deploy_plan: The whole install needs the Workers Paid plan: a sign-in uses more CPU time than the 10 ms per request that Workers Free allows (about 40 ms in our local test).
docs.deploy_step1: 1. Create the database and the bucket
docs.deploy_step1_note: Paste the printed {id} into {file}, and set the route and {default_from} there to your own domain.
docs.deploy_step3_note: {jwt_secret} needs at least 32 characters, {data_key} is base64 of 32 random bytes, and {app_password} (the setup key) needs at least 24 characters. Use three different values and keep a copy of {data_key} and {app_password}. Until {jwt_secret} and {data_key} are valid, sign-in answers 503.
docs.deploy_step4_note: It builds the app, applies pending migrations, then deploys.
docs.deploy_step5_note: Open the app. The Setup screen asks for the setup key ({app_password}) and creates the first admin, with a recovery key to write down.
docs.routing_alt: Mail hosted elsewhere? Run Email Routing on a subdomain instead: see Option B in {doc}.
docs.routing_catchall: Under Routing Rules, use the catch-all rule of the domain with the action {action} and the destination {worker}. Every address of the domain reaches the Worker, which delivers it to the account that owns the address and rejects any other.
docs.routing_from: Everybody sends only from their own primary address.
docs.routing_intro: Mail reaches the app only through Email Routing and leaves through Email Sending. Set up both for each domain you add in the admin console; its {check} button tells you whether a domain is ready.
docs.routing_test: Send a test mail to an account's address from another account. It shows up in that person's Inbox.

domains.guide_in1: In the Cloudflare dashboard open {path} and choose {domain}.
domains.guide_in3: Create a routing rule for one address, with the action {action} and the destination {worker}. To receive every address of the domain, use the catch-all rule with the same action.
domains.guide_in4: Save. Mail for that address now lands in this app. Mail to an address that nobody has here is rejected.
domains.guide_out2: Cloudflare adds the records it needs: MX and SPF on a {bounce} subdomain, a DKIM key, and DMARC on {dmarc}. They can take 5 to 15 minutes to take effect.
domains.guide_out3: Until the domain is onboarded, only verified destination addresses of your Cloudflare account can receive mail; anyone else fails with {code}. Sending to any other recipient also needs the Workers Paid plan.
domains.guide_path_routing: Compute → Email Service → Email Routing → Onboard Domain
domains.guide_path_sending: Compute → Email Service → Email Sending → Onboard Domain
domains.guide_records: Cloudflare adds the MX, SPF and DKIM records on the domain. MX records of another mail provider must be removed first, so that provider stops receiving mail for the domain.
domains.guide_subdomain: A name such as {example} belongs to a domain you already have in Cloudflare. In Email Routing select that main domain, open {settings} and add the subdomain under {subdomains}: Cloudflare adds the records on the subdomain and leaves the main domain's MX alone. Catch-all rules exist only for the main domain, so on a subdomain every address needs its own routing rule, with the action {action} and the destination {worker}. Use a subdomain when the main domain's mail stays with another provider.

security.admin_claim_no_access: No admin can reset another person's password, and there is no way in Edging Mail for an admin to open the mail of someone who has already signed in and set up their keys.
security.admin_claim_operator: Whoever controls the Cloudflare account or the deployed code could change the software.
security.admin_claim_powers: Admins can disable or delete accounts, re-create an address, add or move alias addresses and reset two-factor sign-in; every such change is logged, and the person is told when their two-factor sign-in is reset.
security.admin_claim_setup_key: Whoever holds the setup key can restore an admin's console access with a new key (that admin's old mail stays locked).
security.admin_claim_temp_password: An admin who creates an account knows its temporary password until the person first signs in, and mail that arrives before then is protected only by a server key. So create an account only when the person is ready to sign in.
security.admin_delete_lost_keys: If the person lost both their password and their recovery key, their mail cannot be opened by anyone. Deleting the account and creating it again gives a new, empty mailbox.
security.cannot_turn_off_admin: Admins always use two-factor sign-in, so it cannot be turned off.

setup.err_address_required: Enter the address you will sign in with.
setup.err_name_invalid: Use one line of at most {max} characters.
setup.key_hint: The setup key you set as a secret when you deployed Edging Mail.
setup.lead: Create the first account. It will be the admin, who adds everyone else.
setup.name_hint: Optional. People see it next to your address on messages you send.
setup.not_ready_app_password: APP_PASSWORD is the setup key. You will type it on the next screen.
setup.not_ready_lead: Some secrets are missing from this deployment, so Edging Mail cannot be set up yet.
setup.not_ready_next: Add them as the deployment guide describes, then reload this page.
setup.title: Set up Edging Mail
setup.wrong_key_retry: The setup key was not accepted. Type it again and confirm again: nothing was created, so the recovery key above is still the one to write down.
snooze.too_far: Pick a time within the next year.
snooze.too_soon: Pick a time at least 1 minute from now.
term.subject: Subject
twofa.code_hint: Enter the code the app shows now. If it does not work, wait for the next one and try again.
twofa.codes_keep: Keep them somewhere safe, such as a password manager. This is the only time they are shown.
twofa.codes_lead: If you lose the phone with your authenticator app, a recovery code lets you sign in. Each code works once.
twofa.codes_not_key: Recovery codes are not your recovery key. They cannot restore your mail.
twofa.copy_failed: The text could not be copied. Select it and copy it by hand.
twofa.file_note: Each recovery code works once. Use one to sign in if you cannot use your authenticator app.
twofa.intro: Two-factor sign-in adds a second step when you sign in. An authenticator app on your phone makes a six-digit code that changes every 30 seconds.
twofa.manual_title: Cannot scan it? Enter this key in your app
twofa.qr_failed: The QR code could not be made. Enter the key below in your app instead.
twofa.qr_label: QR code that adds your account to the authenticator app
twofa.saved_check: I have saved these recovery codes
twofa.saved_hint: You cannot see them again after you continue.
twofa.scan_lead: Open your authenticator app and scan this code.
users.alias_hint: Mail sent to these addresses lands in this person's mailbox. They always send from their own address.
users.confirm_demote: They stop being an admin and lose access to the admin console. Their mailbox is not affected.
users.confirm_disable: They are signed out everywhere at once and cannot sign in. Their mail stays and keeps arriving. You can turn the account on again later.
users.confirm_promote_note: They will be asked to set a password of at least 16 characters before they can use the admin console.
users.confirm_reissue: The temporary password this person has now stops working at once. The new one works for {hours} hours. It is shown only once, so send it another way.
users.confirm_reset_two_factor: They are signed out everywhere and set up two-factor sign-in again at their next sign-in. They are told, and so are the other admins. Use this when they lost their phone.
users.confirm_reset_two_factor_admin: The reset takes effect in 24 hours. Until then they can sign in and cancel it. They and the other admins are told now. Use this when they lost their phone.
users.copy_failed: Could not copy. The password is selected: copy it yourself.
users.create_name_hint: Shown to the people they write to. They can change it later.
users.create_no_domain: An account needs an address on one of your domains, and no domain has been added yet.
users.create_password_note: The next screen shows a temporary password for this account. It is shown once.
users.created_give: Give {address} this temporary password. They sign in with it once and then choose their own.
users.created_note_once: It is shown only now. Closing this window loses it.
users.created_note_send: Send it another way, not to this new address: the person cannot read that mailbox yet.
users.delete_body: This deletes {address} with all of its mail, drafts, attachments and settings. It cannot be undone.
users.delete_key_note: People who write to them will be asked to confirm the new key.
users.err_alias_incomplete: Enter a full address, such as sales@example.com.
users.err_local_chars: Use only letters a to z, digits, dots, hyphens and underscores.
users.err_local_dots: No dot at the start or end, and no two dots in a row.
users.reset_scheduled: The reset is scheduled for {due}. The person can sign in before then to cancel it.
users.self_note: You cannot disable, delete or reset the two-factor sign-in of your own account here.
